title: Mark Chapter 14 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Mark chapter 14 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Mark Chapter 14 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Mark Chapter 14.

questions.question: In Mark 14, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The chief priests and scribes seek how to take Jesus by craft
A woman breaks an alabaster box of ointment on Jesus' head
Judas Iscariot goes to the chief priests to betray Jesus
Jesus takes bread and breaks it saying, 'this is my body'
questions.correctAnswer: The chief priests and scribes seek how to take Jesus by craft
questions.explanation: Mark 14:1 describes the chief priests and scribes seeking how to take Jesus by craft first in the chapter.

questions.question: Where was Jesus when the woman broke the alabaster box of ointment on his head?
options: In Bethany in the house of Simon the leper
In Jerusalem at the temple
In the upper room in the city
At the feast of the passover
questions.correctAnswer: In Bethany in the house of Simon the leper
questions.explanation: Mark 14:3 states Jesus was in Bethany in the house of Simon the leper when the woman broke the alabaster box.

questions.question: What did some people say about the ointment poured on Jesus?
options: Why was this waste of the ointment made?
It was the best ointment ever used
It should be saved for another time
It was not enough for Jesus
questions.correctAnswer: Why was this waste of the ointment made?
questions.explanation: Mark 14:4 records that some had indignation and said, 'Why was this waste of the ointment made?'

questions.question: How much did the ointment used on Jesus cost according to the murmurers?
options: More than three hundred pence
Fifty pence
One hundred pence
Ten pence
questions.correctAnswer: More than three hundred pence
questions.explanation: Mark 14:5 states the ointment might have been sold for more than three hundred pence and given to the poor.

questions.question: What did Jesus say about the poor when defending the woman?
options: The poor ye have always with you
The poor shall be taken care of later
The poor shall be blessed first
The poor will be healed soon
questions.correctAnswer: The poor ye have always with you
questions.explanation: Mark 14:7 quotes Jesus saying, 'For ye have the poor with you always,' defending the woman's act.

questions.question: What did Jesus say the woman was anointing in advance?
options: His body to the burying
His feet before washing
His hands for healing
His head for the feast
questions.correctAnswer: His body to the burying
questions.explanation: Mark 14:8 states she came beforehand to anoint Jesus' body to the burying.

questions.question: What did Jesus say would be spoken of wherever the gospel is preached?
options: The deed of the woman pouring ointment
The betrayal by Judas Iscariot
The feast of the passover
The breaking of the bread
questions.correctAnswer: The deed of the woman pouring ointment
questions.explanation: Mark 14:9 says that her deed shall be spoken of for a memorial wherever the gospel is preached.

questions.question: Who went to the chief priests to betray Jesus?
options: Judas Iscariot
Peter
John
Thomas
questions.correctAnswer: Judas Iscariot
questions.explanation: Mark 14:10 states Judas Iscariot, one of the twelve, went to the chief priests to betray Jesus.

questions.question: What did the chief priests do when they heard Judas' plan to betray Jesus?
options: They were glad and promised to give him money
They warned Jesus immediately
They sent soldiers to arrest Jesus
They called a meeting of the twelve
questions.correctAnswer: They were glad and promised to give him money
questions.explanation: Mark 14:11 says the chief priests were glad and promised Judas money when they heard his plan.

questions.question: What did Jesus instruct two disciples to do on the first day of unleavened bread?
options: Go into the city and follow a man bearing a pitcher of water
Buy lambs for the passover
Prepare the meal at Simon's house
Wait for the signal from Jesus
questions.correctAnswer: Go into the city and follow a man bearing a pitcher of water
questions.explanation: Mark 14:13 records Jesus sending two disciples to follow a man bearing a pitcher of water in the city.

questions.question: What will the man with the pitcher of water show the disciples?
options: A large upper room furnished and prepared
A secret garden
An empty street
A place to buy unleavened bread
questions.correctAnswer: A large upper room furnished and prepared
questions.explanation: Mark 14:15 states the man will show them a large upper room furnished and prepared for the passover.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus said one of the twelve who ate with Him would betray Him.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Mark 14:18 records Jesus saying that one of the twelve who ate with Him would betray Him.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus said it would be better for the man who betrays Him if he had never been born.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Mark 14:21 explicitly states Jesus said it would be better for the betrayer if he had never been born.

questions.question: True or False: The text says Jesus was betrayed by Peter.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Mark 14:10-11 identifies Judas Iscariot as the betrayer, not Peter.

questions.question: True or False: The text says Jesus was anointed with oil after the passover meal.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Mark 14:3 shows the woman anointed Jesus before the passover meal, not after.

medium.title: Mark Chapter 14 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Mark Chapter 14 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did Jesus say about drinking the fruit of the vine?
options: I will drink it new in the kingdom of God.
I will drink it daily.
I will never drink it again.
I will drink it with the prophets.
questions.correctAnswer: I will drink it new in the kingdom of God.
questions.explanation: This is stated in Mark 14:25, where Jesus promises that he will not drink of the fruit of the vine until he drinks it new in God's kingdom.

questions.question: What does Mark 14:26 promise will happen if someone sings a hymn?
options: They will go out into the mount of Olives.
They will be filled with joy.
They will receive blessings.
They will be forgiven.
questions.correctAnswer: They will go out into the mount of Olives.
questions.explanation: Mark 14:26 states that after they sang a hymn, they went out into the mount of Olives, indicating the next step after worship.

questions.question: What did Jesus predict would happen to his disciples that night?
options: They would deny him.
They would flee to safety.
They would remain faithful.
They would sing hymns.
questions.correctAnswer: They would deny him.
questions.explanation: In Mark 14:27, Jesus foretells that all his disciples would be offended and scatter, indicating their denial.

questions.question: What assurance does Mark 14:28 give about Jesus after his resurrection?
options: He will return to Jerusalem.
He will go before them into Galilee.
He will ascend to heaven immediately.
He will reveal himself in the temple.
questions.correctAnswer: He will go before them into Galilee.
questions.explanation: Mark 14:28 assures the disciples that after his resurrection, Jesus will lead them to Galilee, providing hope for their future.

questions.question: What does Mark 14:30 reveal about Peter's denial?
options: He will deny Jesus thrice before the cock crows twice.
He will never deny Jesus.
He will deny Jesus only once.
He will deny Jesus after the resurrection.
questions.correctAnswer: He will deny Jesus thrice before the cock crows twice.
questions.explanation: Mark 14:30 records Jesus telling Peter he will deny him three times before the rooster crows twice, highlighting the gravity of Peter's coming failure.

questions.question: In Mark 14:31, what did Peter insist regarding his loyalty to Jesus?
options: He would die with Jesus.
He would deny Jesus.
He would run away.
He would betray Jesus.
questions.correctAnswer: He would die with Jesus.
questions.explanation: Peter vehemently claims in Mark 14:31 that even if he should die with Jesus, he would not deny Him, showcasing his strong, yet misguided, commitment.

questions.question: What did Jesus ask his disciples to do while he prayed in Gethsemane?
options: Sit ye here, while I shall pray.
Go to sleep.
Sing hymns.
Gather strength.
questions.correctAnswer: Sit ye here, while I shall pray.
questions.explanation: Mark 14:32 states that Jesus instructed his disciples to sit while he went to pray, indicating a moment of solitude and prayer.

questions.question: In Mark 14:34, how did Jesus describe his emotional state?
options: Joyful and hopeful.
Exceeding sorrowful unto death.
Calm and composed.
Angry and frustrated.
questions.correctAnswer: Exceeding sorrowful unto death.
questions.explanation: Mark 14:34 records Jesus expressing deep sorrow and anguish, indicating the heavy burden he was bearing as he approached the crucifixion.

questions.question: What does Mark 14:38 warn about the spirit and the flesh?
options: The spirit is weak, but the flesh is strong.
The spirit truly is ready, but the flesh is weak.
The spirit and flesh are equal.
The flesh is ready, but the spirit is weak.
questions.correctAnswer: The spirit truly is ready, but the flesh is weak.
questions.explanation: Mark 14:38 emphasizes the struggle between the readiness of the spirit and the weakness of the flesh, reminding believers of their need for vigilance.

questions.question: What did Jesus say when he found his disciples sleeping in Mark 14:37?
options: Sleep on now, and take your rest.
Why are you sleeping?
Awake and pray!
I need your help.
questions.correctAnswer: Sleep on now, and take your rest.
questions.explanation: In Mark 14:37, Jesus addresses Peter and indicates that they can continue sleeping, marking a moment of resignation to their weakness.

questions.question: What was the significance of Judas's kiss according to Mark 14:44?
options: It was a sign of loyalty.
It was a token for betrayal.
It was a greeting of peace.
It was a sign of friendship.
questions.correctAnswer: It was a token for betrayal.
questions.explanation: Mark 14:44 reveals that Judas used a kiss as a signal to identify Jesus to the authorities, marking the ultimate act of betrayal.

questions.question: What does Mark 14:48 indicate about how Jesus was treated by those who came to arrest him?
options: He was treated as a thief.
He was treated with respect.
He was greeted warmly.
He was ignored.
questions.correctAnswer: He was treated as a thief.
questions.explanation: In Mark 14:48, Jesus questions the manner of his arrest, pointing out that they came against him as if he were a criminal, highlighting the injustice of the situation.

questions.question: Is it true that Jesus prayed for the cup to be taken away from him?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: In Mark 14:36, Jesus asks the Father to take away the cup from him, expressing his anguish while ultimately submitting to God's will.

questions.question: Is it true that the disciples were fully alert while Jesus prayed?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Mark 14:40 states that the disciples were found sleeping again, showing their inability to stay awake and watch as Jesus asked.

questions.question: Is it true that Peter drew a sword and attacked the high priest's servant?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Mark 14:47 mentions that one of them drew a sword and cut off a servant's ear, but it does not explicitly say it was Peter who did so.

hard.title: Mark Chapter 14 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Mark Chapter 14.

questions.question: What reason does Jesus give for why the authorities did not seize Him earlier in the temple?
options: The scriptures must be fulfilled
They feared the people
He was protected by the temple guards
It was not yet the appointed hour
questions.correctAnswer: The scriptures must be fulfilled
questions.explanation: Mark 14:49 shows Jesus saying, 'I was daily with you in the temple teaching, and ye took me not: but the scriptures must be fulfilled.' This indicates the necessity of fulfilling scripture was why He was not seized earlier.

questions.question: What happened to Jesus' followers at the moment He was arrested?
options: They all forsook Him and fled
They fought to defend Him
They were arrested alongside Him
They stayed close but silent
questions.correctAnswer: They all forsook Him and fled
questions.explanation: Mark 14:50 states, 'And they all forsook him, and fled,' demonstrating that all His followers deserted Him at His arrest.

questions.question: Who followed Jesus after His arrest while only wrapped in a linen cloth?
options: A certain young man
Peter
John the beloved disciple
Judas Iscariot
questions.correctAnswer: A certain young man
questions.explanation: Mark 14:51 describes 'a certain young man, having a linen cloth cast about his naked body' following Jesus, indicating a mysterious figure distinct from the named disciples.

questions.question: What did the young man do when the arresting men tried to seize him?
options: He left the linen cloth and fled naked
He fought back with a sword
He pleaded for mercy
He was captured along with Jesus
questions.correctAnswer: He left the linen cloth and fled naked
questions.explanation: Mark 14:52 records, 'And he left the linen cloth, and fled from them naked,' showing his escape strategy was to flee without his garment.

questions.question: Who gathered together at the high priest's house when Jesus was led there?
options: All the chief priests, elders, and scribes
Only the chief priests
The Roman soldiers
The disciples and Jesus' family
questions.correctAnswer: All the chief priests, elders, and scribes
questions.explanation: Mark 14:53 states, 'and with him were assembled all the chief priests and the elders and the scribes,' indicating a full religious council was present.

questions.question: Where was Peter when Jesus was taken to the high priest, and what was he doing?
options: In the palace, sitting with the servants and warming himself at the fire
Outside the palace, praying fervently
In the temple, teaching the people
With the disciples, hiding in fear
questions.correctAnswer: In the palace, sitting with the servants and warming himself at the fire
questions.explanation: Mark 14:54 describes Peter following 'afar off, even into the palace of the high priest: and he sat with the servants, and warmed himself at the fire.'

questions.question: What is the meaning of the Greek word 'ἐγκαταλείπω' (egkataleipō) used in Mark 14:50?
options: To forsake or abandon
To follow closely
To accuse falsely
To speak loudly
questions.correctAnswer: To forsake or abandon
questions.explanation: The Greek word 'ἐγκαταλείπω' in Mark 14:50 means 'to forsake or abandon,' which fits the context of the disciples leaving Jesus and fleeing.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Mark 14:62 when Jesus declares 'I am; and ye shall see the Son of man sitting on the right hand of power'?
options: Allusion
Metaphor
Simile
Irony
questions.correctAnswer: Allusion
questions.explanation: Mark 14:62 alludes to Daniel 7:13-14, where the 'Son of man' comes with clouds of heaven, thus employing allusion to Old Testament prophecy.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage connects to Jesus' statement in Mark 14:27 about the shepherd being smitten and the sheep scattered?
options: Zechariah 13:7
Isaiah 53:4
Psalm 22:1
Genesis 3:15
questions.correctAnswer: Zechariah 13:7
questions.explanation: Mark 14:27 quotes Zechariah 13:7, 'I will smite the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered,' linking Jesus' prediction to this prophetic scripture.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage fulfills Jesus' prediction in Mark 14:30 about Peter denying Him thrice before the cock crows twice?
options: John 18:27
Acts 2:14
Luke 22:61
Matthew 26:74
questions.correctAnswer: John 18:27
questions.explanation: John 18:27 records Peter's denial of Jesus before the cock crowed, fulfilling the prediction in Mark 14:30.

questions.question: What event immediately precedes the statement in Mark 14:49 where Jesus mentions being daily with the people in the temple teaching?
options: The arrest of Jesus by the chief priests and scribes
The Last Supper with the disciples
Jesus praying in Gethsemane
Peter's denial of Jesus
questions.correctAnswer: The arrest of Jesus by the chief priests and scribes
questions.explanation: Mark 14:48 describes Jesus being taken by force, immediately preceding His statement in Mark 14:49 about daily teaching in the temple.

questions.question: What is the significance of the linen cloth mentioned in Mark 14:51-52 in the cultural context of first-century Judea?
options: It was a common burial cloth symbolizing vulnerability
It was a priestly garment indicating religious authority
It was a symbol of wealth and status
It was a Roman soldier's uniform
questions.correctAnswer: It was a common burial cloth symbolizing vulnerability
questions.explanation: The linen cloth likely refers to a simple garment or burial cloth, and the young man's fleeing naked symbolizes vulnerability and abandonment (Mark 14:51-52).

questions.question: How do the false witnesses against Jesus in Mark 14:56-59 illustrate the legal challenges in His trial?
options: Their testimonies did not agree, highlighting the unreliability of the accusations
They unanimously condemned Him, showing a unified case
They presented physical evidence against Him
They called for a Roman trial instead
questions.correctAnswer: Their testimonies did not agree, highlighting the unreliability of the accusations
questions.explanation: Mark 14:56-59 shows many bore false witness but their testimonies did not agree, underscoring the lack of credible evidence in the trial.

questions.question: Which typological parallel is seen in Peter's denial of Jesus in Mark 14:66-72?
options: Peter as the 'sheep' scattered after the shepherd is struck
Peter as a new Moses leading Israel
Peter as the Davidic king
Peter as the faithful Elijah
questions.correctAnswer: Peter as the 'sheep' scattered after the shepherd is struck
questions.explanation: Peter's denial fulfills Jesus' prediction in Mark 14:27 about the shepherd being struck and the sheep scattered, typologically linking Peter to the scattered sheep.

questions.question: True or False: According to Mark 14:64, the council condemned Jesus to death on the charge of blasphemy.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Mark 14:64 states, 'Ye have heard the blasphemy: what think ye? And they all condemned him to be guilty of death,' confirming the charge was blasphemy.

theological.title: Mark Chapter 14 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Mark Chapter 14 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Mark 14:8 teach about salvation?
options: Christ’s anointing anticipates His sacrificial death and burial
Salvation comes through human works and offerings
The poor are always prioritized over Jesus in salvation
Anointing is a ritual for cleansing sin
questions.correctAnswer: Christ’s anointing anticipates His sacrificial death and burial
questions.explanation: Mark 14:8 states, 'She hath done what she could: she is come aforehand to anoint my body to the burying,' teaching that the anointing foreshadows Christ’s impending death and burial, a key aspect of salvation.

questions.question: What doctrine does Mark 14:24 teach about the new covenant?
options: Christ’s blood inaugurates the new testament, shed for many
The new covenant is based on human obedience to the law
The new testament replaces the old covenant without continuity
Jesus’ blood is symbolic but not efficacious for salvation
questions.correctAnswer: Christ’s blood inaugurates the new testament, shed for many
questions.explanation: Mark 14:24 says, 'This is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many,' teaching that Jesus’ sacrificial blood establishes the new covenant for salvation.

questions.question: What doctrine about human sin is taught in Mark 14:30?
options: Even the closest disciples will fall into sin through denial
True believers cannot sin or fall away
Denial is a minor failing without consequence
Peter’s denial was predestined and unavoidable
questions.correctAnswer: Even the closest disciples will fall into sin through denial
questions.explanation: In Mark 14:30, Jesus predicts Peter’s denial, showing that human sinfulness affects even the most faithful followers.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Mark 14:36 specifically demonstrate?
options: Submission to the Father’s will despite personal anguish
Omnipotence in overcoming temptation
Immutability in divine nature
Justice in punishing sin
questions.correctAnswer: Submission to the Father’s will despite personal anguish
questions.explanation: Mark 14:36 shows Jesus praying, 'not what I will, but what thou wilt,' demonstrating His submission and obedience to the Father’s will.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated by Jesus’ knowledge in Mark 14:21?
options: Omniscience in foretelling His betrayal
Mercy in forgiving sinners unconditionally
Wrath in condemning the betrayer
Sovereignty in controlling all events
questions.correctAnswer: Omniscience in foretelling His betrayal
questions.explanation: Mark 14:21 records Jesus predicting His betrayal and its consequences, showing His divine omniscience.

questions.question: How does Mark 14:22–24 connect to the broader biblical theme of covenant renewal?
options: It inaugurates the new covenant through Christ’s body and blood
It contrasts with Old Testament sacrifices as insufficient
It abolishes all covenant promises made to Israel
It establishes a legalistic covenant based on works
questions.correctAnswer: It inaugurates the new covenant through Christ’s body and blood
questions.explanation: These verses correspond with Jeremiah’s prophecy of a new covenant and represent its inauguration through Jesus’ sacrifice.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection is seen in Mark 14:27 regarding the scattering of the sheep?
options: It fulfills Zechariah’s prophecy about the shepherd being struck
It contradicts Old Testament expectations for the Messiah
It depicts the permanent abandonment of Israel by God
It symbolizes the final judgment on the nations
questions.correctAnswer: It fulfills Zechariah’s prophecy about the shepherd being struck
questions.explanation: Mark 14:27 quotes Zechariah 13:7 about the shepherd being struck and sheep scattered, connecting Jesus’ passion to prophetic fulfillment.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Mark 14:42 and Mark 14:44 teach about divine sovereignty and human responsibility?
options: Jesus knowingly submits to betrayal while Judas acts out of his own choice
Betrayal occurs without any divine foreknowledge or purpose
Human actors are mere puppets without any responsibility
God forces Judas to betray Jesus against his will
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus knowingly submits to betrayal while Judas acts out of his own choice
questions.explanation: Mark 14:42 shows Jesus aware of the betrayal hour, and 14:44 shows Judas’s active betrayal, illustrating coexistence of divine sovereignty and human responsibility.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Mark 14:61–62 and Mark 14:63–64 teach about Christ’s identity and blasphemy?
options: Jesus affirms His divine Sonship, leading to a charge of blasphemy
Jesus denies being the Messiah to avoid death
The high priest recognizes Jesus as a true prophet
Jesus claims to be a political revolutionary
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus affirms His divine Sonship, leading to a charge of blasphemy
questions.explanation: In Mark 14:61–62 Jesus declares Himself the Son of man seated at God’s right hand; 14:63–64 shows the high priest accusing Him of blasphemy for this claim.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Mark 14:37 and Mark 14:38 teach about the tension between spirit and flesh in sanctification?
options: The spirit desires faithfulness, but the flesh is weak and prone to failure
Human nature is inherently good and untempted
Prayer is unnecessary since the spirit is always ready
Fleshly weakness excuses sin without need for vigilance
questions.correctAnswer: The spirit desires faithfulness, but the flesh is weak and prone to failure
questions.explanation: Mark 14:37–38 reveals Jesus rebuking sleeping disciples, emphasizing the struggle between a willing spirit and weak flesh needing prayer and watchfulness.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Mark 14:55–59 shows the trial was rigged with false testimony. What does Mark 14:55–59 actually teach?
options: False witnesses were presented but their testimonies did not agree
The trial was fair and based on unanimous truthful evidence
Jesus was innocent but confessed guilt voluntarily
The council immediately found enough true witnesses to convict
questions.correctAnswer: False witnesses were presented but their testimonies did not agree
questions.explanation: Mark 14:55–59 states many bore false witness but their testimonies did not agree, showing the trial’s weakness in evidence.

questions.question: What doctrine does Mark 14:7 teach about the permanence of the poor versus Christ’s temporal presence?
options: The poor will always be present, but Jesus’ earthly presence is limited
The poor are less important than Jesus and can be neglected
Jesus will always be physically present with believers
Charitable giving is unnecessary because of Christ’s return
questions.correctAnswer: The poor will always be present, but Jesus’ earthly presence is limited
questions.explanation: Mark 14:7 explains, 'ye have the poor with you always, and whensoever ye will ye may do them good: but me ye have not always,' indicating Jesus’ temporary physical presence.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is displayed in Jesus’ calm rebuke in Mark 14:48 when arrested?
options: Sovereignty over unjust human actions
Impatience with human weakness
Wrath against His enemies
Indifference to His fate
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty over unjust human actions
questions.explanation: Mark 14:48 shows Jesus questioning the arrest with authority and control, demonstrating divine sovereignty even in suffering.

questions.question: How does Mark 14:72 contribute to the narrative arc of Peter’s restoration in the New Testament?
options: It marks the beginning of Peter’s repentance and eventual restoration
It shows Peter’s permanent rejection by Jesus
It depicts Peter as an example of unrepentant sin
It ends Peter’s role as a disciple
questions.correctAnswer: It marks the beginning of Peter’s repentance and eventual restoration
questions.explanation: Mark 14:72 records Peter weeping after denying Jesus, indicating genuine sorrow that leads to his restoration (cf. John 21).

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Mark 14:18 and Mark 14:19 teach about Jesus’ knowledge and the disciples’ human frailty?
options: Jesus knows the betrayal is imminent; disciples respond with sorrow and confusion
The disciples are fully aware and prepared for betrayal
Jesus is uncertain about who will betray Him
The betrayal is a surprise to both Jesus and the disciples
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus knows the betrayal is imminent; disciples respond with sorrow and confusion
questions.explanation: Mark 14:18 records Jesus’ foreknowledge of betrayal; 14:19 shows disciples distressed and questioning themselves, revealing human frailty.
